_doc: PRO story graph design (skeleton for review, not generated). ages = requires min/max age; seasons_with_club = seasons with the current club (the count restarts at every new club); kind: once / variant (age-banded) / repeat (re-fires with cooldown); waits_on = gameplay requests R1-R7 (consolidated code request to the gameplay session); callbacks = HS/college flags read only by locked choices. Pro strike flags: pro_night_out, pro_unapproved_supplement, pro_bar_fight, pro_shared_inside_info, pro_party_house, pro_reckless_driving, pro_online_rant, pro_gambling_debt, stayed_out_pro. relationship_strike_flags: the relationship wrong path (cheating); separate from the pro strikes, never read by the team-discipline steps. Partner flags: made_long_distance_work / committed_to_relationship (the high school love interest), new_partner (after Someone New), engaged, married; breakups clear them and set broke_up_pro or divorced.

requests.R4: transition flags + right-now metrics (landed: slump_now, benched_now, injured_now, fg_streak, season_fg_pct, pro_seasons, contract_years_left, clubs; flags contract_year, re_signed, released, signed_new_club)

scenarios.title: Rookie Camp
scenarios.premise: Camp opens with four kickers on the roster and one job. The veteran special teams coordinator calls you by the wrong name twice.

scenarios.title: The Veteran Kicker
scenarios.premise: The kicker whose job you're taking has been here eleven years. He can make your first month easy or impossible.

scenarios.title: The First Check
scenarios.premise: Your first real paycheck lands, and it has more zeros than {parent} made in a year.

scenarios.title: Rookie Duties
scenarios.premise: The veterans hand the rookies a list: breakfast for the unit every Friday, the luggage, the karaoke on the team plane. Some of it is fun. One item isn't.

scenarios.title: The Long Snapper
scenarios.premise: The long snapper has been in the league fourteen years and has opinions about everything, including your warmup.

scenarios.title: The First Road Trip
scenarios.premise: First road trip. Curfew is eleven, and the veterans say curfew is for rookies who want to stay rookies.
scenarios.note: Pressure scene: clean no. The wrong choice sets pro strike stayed_out_pro.

scenarios.title: Where You Live
scenarios.premise: Half the roster lives in the same glass tower downtown. The rent is a quarter of your salary.

scenarios.title: Homesick in {town}
scenarios.premise: Nobody in {town} knows your name yet, and the apartment is very quiet on Tuesday nights.

scenarios.title: The Practice Squad Friend
scenarios.premise: The receiver you've been eating lunch with since camp gets cut on a Tuesday morning. He's still in the parking lot at noon.

scenarios.title: Meeting the Owner
scenarios.premise: The owner throws a party for the rookies at his house and spends twenty minutes telling you what kickers are worth.

scenarios.title: The Quote
scenarios.premise: You said something careless to a beat reporter about the veteran you replaced, and it's the headline.

scenarios.title: Your First Autograph Line
scenarios.premise: A kid in a jersey with your number on it is first in line. You didn't know they made your number.

scenarios.title: Rookie Year Ends
scenarios.premise: The season's over. The locker room empties in an afternoon, and you realize you have no idea what pros do in the offseason.

scenarios.title: The Second-Year Wall
scenarios.premise: Year two. The novelty is gone, the scouting reports on you are thicker, and your legs feel every one of last season's kicks.

scenarios.title: The Rookie Symposium Call
scenarios.premise: A former teammate from college calls from his rookie symposium: they told a story about someone who sounds a lot like you.
scenarios.note: College callback scene: opens only for players with a college comeback; pairs with pro_rookie_symposium.

scenarios.title: The Slump
scenarios.premise: Three weeks of misses in practice and the coaches have stopped talking to you about it, which is worse.
scenarios.note: Repeatable (cooldown 15 weeks). Locks open with experience (kick_slumps, age).

scenarios.title: The Coach Loses Faith
scenarios.premise: {coach} watches your warmup with folded arms and doesn't say a word.

scenarios.title: Benched
scenarios.premise: You're inactive this week. Your name is on the board, and your helmet is in your locker.
scenarios.note: Every engine flag is sticky from high school, so the present-state check is needed.

scenarios.title: The Job Back
scenarios.premise: You're active again. The kicker who replaced you is clearing out his stall.

scenarios.title: The Hot Streak
scenarios.premise: You haven't missed in a month, and everyone wants to talk about it except you.

scenarios.title: Don't Talk About It
scenarios.premise: The specialists have a superstition: nobody says the streak out loud. A rookie just said it.

scenarios.title: The Watch List
scenarios.premise: Your name is on the national list for the league's best kicker, and the team's PR staff has eleven requests for you.

scenarios.title: The Skills Contest
scenarios.premise: The league invites you to the long-distance contest at the all-star week.
scenarios.note: kick_challenge (competition) per the gameplay handoff.

scenarios.title: Talk Radio
scenarios.premise: The afternoon talk show has a segment called 'Cut the Kicker', and your {parent} listens to it every day.

scenarios.title: The Yips
scenarios.premise: Your foot won't swing through the ball in practice. Not tired, not hurt, just stuck.

scenarios.title: The Private Kicking Coach
scenarios.premise: A private coach who rebuilt three pro kickers offers you his offseason, for a price.

scenarios.title: The Film That Hurts
scenarios.premise: {coach} plays every miss of your season back to back in an empty meeting room.

scenarios.title: Kicking Hurt
scenarios.premise: Your plant leg is sore in a way the trainers can't find on a scan.

scenarios.title: The Backup Wants Your Job
scenarios.premise: {backup} is on the practice squad and has been kicking very well where the coaches can see.

scenarios.title: The New Holder Midseason
scenarios.premise: {holder} is hurt, and the replacement holder is a backup quarterback who has never held for a kick.

scenarios.title: The Incentive Clause
scenarios.premise: Your contract pays a bonus if you hit 90 percent this season, and your agent keeps texting you the math.

scenarios.title: The Kicker Brought In
scenarios.premise: The club signs a kicker with a bigger leg and a lower salary, and puts him at the locker next to yours.
scenarios.note: Prime-age version; PRO_133 is the veteran version.

scenarios.title: Playing for a Contract
scenarios.premise: Every kick in practice now feels like a negotiation.

scenarios.title: The Kick Everyone Saw
scenarios.premise: A clip of you in a practice-field trick shot goes around the league.
scenarios.note: Practice clip only; no game result.

scenarios.title: The Bad Week
scenarios.premise: You snapped at {holder}, ignored {coach} and skipped the team meal. It's been that kind of week.

scenarios.title: Contract Year: Prove It
scenarios.premise: It's the last year of your rookie deal, and the front office wants to see one more season before they talk.

scenarios.title: Contract Year: The Payday
scenarios.premise: This is the contract that sets up your family for life, if you earn it this season.

scenarios.title: Contract Year: One More
scenarios.premise: At your age, the next contract is one year at a time, and everyone in the building knows it.

scenarios.title: The Re-Sign Call
scenarios.premise: The club wants you back. Your agent wants to wait for the market.

scenarios.title: The Hometown Discount
scenarios.premise: The club offers less than the market, and asks you to take it because you're family here.

scenarios.title: The Holdout Talk
scenarios.premise: Your agent says the only way to get paid is to stay home from camp.
scenarios.note: A temptation, not a mechanic: the game has no holdouts. Holding firm costs retention and the coach.

scenarios.title: Starting Over
scenarios.premise: The last club let you go. A week ago you were cleaning out a locker; today you're in a stranger's locker room in a city you've never visited.
scenarios.note: Opens after any release or cut (the engine's failed_tryouts list), in the first weeks at the next club. Tone-check scene (being cut at the end of camp).
uses: R4 released (failed_tryouts is also set by a failed college walk-on tryout)

scenarios.title: New Club, New Locker Room
scenarios.premise: First day at {club}. Your name is on tape above a locker that still has someone else's sticker on it.

scenarios.title: The New Holder
scenarios.premise: {holder} spins the laces differently than anyone you've worked with.

scenarios.title: Moving the Family
scenarios.premise: The new contract is in {town}. Your partner has a job and friends where you live now.

scenarios.title: The Family Stays Behind
scenarios.premise: You'll be in {town} during the season, and your family will be a flight away.

scenarios.title: Your Old Team Comes to Town
scenarios.premise: Your old club is on the schedule. Half the locker room over there still texts you.

scenarios.title: The Agent's Bigger Client
scenarios.premise: Your agent just signed a star quarterback, and your calls go to voicemail.

scenarios.title: Firing Your Agent
scenarios.premise: Your agent has missed two deadlines this year. Firing him means starting over with someone new.

scenarios.title: The Good Agent
scenarios.premise: An agent with six clients asks for an hour to show you a plan with no flash in it at all.

scenarios.title: The Tryout Hotel
scenarios.premise: You got the job at a Tuesday tryout. Now you live in a hotel by the airport until somebody says otherwise.

scenarios.title: The Teammate Traded Away
scenarios.premise: The club traded your holder's best friend at midnight. He found out from his phone.
scenarios.note: Other players get traded; the player can't be.

scenarios.title: The Head Coach Is Fired
scenarios.premise: The head coach is fired after a team meeting. {coach}'s office lights are on late.

scenarios.title: The General Manager's Nephew
scenarios.premise: The new general manager is the owner's nephew, and he has opinions about kickers.

scenarios.title: Loyalty or the Paycheck
scenarios.premise: Another club would pay you double. This one gave you your first chance.

scenarios.title: The Big Check
scenarios.premise: The signing bonus clears. Your phone lights up with cousins.

scenarios.title: The Honest Advisor
scenarios.premise: A financial advisor recommended by your snapper walks you through a plan so boring it's almost funny.

scenarios.title: The Advisor With the Yacht
scenarios.premise: A financial advisor who manages three teammates invites you onto his boat and talks about 'real returns'.

scenarios.title: The Missing Money
scenarios.premise: Your accounts are lighter than they should be, and the advisor isn't answering.
scenarios.note: Works now with flags and stress; the stolen 40% lands with R3.

scenarios.title: The Lawsuit
scenarios.premise: Your lawyer says you can sue the advisor. It'll take three years and your name will be in every story.

scenarios.title: The Restaurant
scenarios.premise: An old college teammate wants your name and your money on a steakhouse downtown. He has a chef, a location and a business plan he wrote last night.

scenarios.title: The Restaurant Is Failing
scenarios.premise: The steakhouse is losing money every week, and your name is on the sign.

scenarios.title: The Car Dealership
scenarios.premise: A dealership wants you as a partner: your face on the billboards, your money in the lot.

scenarios.title: The Friend's Start-Up
scenarios.premise: {best_friend} is starting a company and asks you to be the first investor.

scenarios.title: The Start-Up Calls
scenarios.premise: {best_friend}'s company is either about to make it or about to fold, and they need one more check.
scenarios.note: The one good venture: it can pay off.

scenarios.title: The Tax Letter, Pro
scenarios.premise: You owe taxes in every state you played a road game in, and your old accountant didn't file most of them.

scenarios.title: Family Asks for Money
scenarios.premise: {sibling} needs money and doesn't want {parent} to know.

scenarios.title: The Cousin Nobody Remembers
scenarios.premise: Someone from your hometown with your last name and a business idea is waiting by your car.

scenarios.title: {parent}'s House
scenarios.premise: You could pay off {parent}'s mortgage this week. He's told you not to, twice.

scenarios.title: The Foundation
scenarios.premise: Your charity foundation's director is spending more on galas than on kids.

scenarios.title: The Watch, the Car, the Chain
scenarios.premise: The locker room has a dress code nobody wrote down, and it costs about your rookie salary.

scenarios.title: Broke at Thirty-Three
scenarios.premise: The money's gone faster than the career, and you have a mortgage, a family and maybe three seasons.

scenarios.title: The Pension Meeting
scenarios.premise: The players' union holds a meeting about pensions and retirement plans. Six players show up.

scenarios.title: The Proposal
scenarios.premise: You've been carrying a ring around for three weeks, waiting for the right moment that won't come during a season.

scenarios.title: The Wedding
scenarios.premise: The wedding is in the offseason. The guest list is a fight.

scenarios.title: The Due Date
scenarios.premise: The baby is due the same week as a road game across the country.

scenarios.title: First Day of School
scenarios.premise: Your kid's first day of school is a Thursday practice.

scenarios.title: The Recital
scenarios.premise: A school recital, a road trip, and a kid who has asked three times if you'll be there.

scenarios.title: Your Partner's Career
scenarios.premise: Your partner has been offered the job of a lifetime, in a city with no team.

scenarios.title: {parent} Is Getting Older
scenarios.premise: {parent} forgets the name of a neighbor he's known for twenty years.

scenarios.title: {parent}'s Last Season in the Stands
scenarios.premise: {parent} says this is the last season he'll make the drive to watch you.

scenarios.title: {sibling}'s Own Shot
scenarios.premise: {sibling} has a tryout of his own, and he wants you there.

scenarios.title: The Old Friend's Ticket Requests
scenarios.premise: {best_friend} asks for tickets every week and brings a different stranger every time.
scenarios.note: Repeatable (cooldown 15-20 weeks).

scenarios.title: The Coach Who Taught You
scenarios.premise: Your high school coach is retiring, and the school wants you to speak at the dinner.

scenarios.title: {tyler} in the Same Division
scenarios.premise: {tyler} signs with a division rival, and the media has already made the graphic.

scenarios.title: {tyler} Gets Cut
scenarios.premise: {tyler} is released on a Monday. He calls you before his agent.

scenarios.title: {tyler}'s Second Act
scenarios.premise: {tyler} is in the broadcast booth now, and he's calling your games.

scenarios.title: The Rookie Kicker You Mentor
scenarios.premise: The club drafts a kicker and asks you to show the rookie how things work, knowing what that means.

scenarios.title: The Mentee Takes Your Job
scenarios.premise: The kicker you taught is better than you now, and {coach} wants to tell you before the depth chart comes out.

scenarios.title: The Holder's Last Season
scenarios.premise: {holder} is retiring after this season and wants every hold to count.

scenarios.title: The Snapper Retires
scenarios.premise: The long snapper you've trusted for years is done, and he asks you to speak at his farewell.

scenarios.title: A Teammate in Trouble
scenarios.premise: A teammate's arrest is on every channel. He asks you to vouch for him at the hearing.
scenarios.note: Repeatable (cooldown 15-20 weeks).

scenarios.title: The Concussion
scenarios.premise: A teammate who has had too many concussions is hiding another one, and you saw it happen.

scenarios.title: The Letter From a Kid
scenarios.premise: A letter from a kid in a hospital you visited years ago: he's walking now.

scenarios.title: The Tabloid
scenarios.premise: A gossip site prints a story about your marriage that's mostly made up.

scenarios.title: The Marriage on the Road
scenarios.premise: You've been home eleven nights since August, and your partner has stopped asking when you'll be back.

scenarios.title: The Reunion
scenarios.premise: Your high school reunion is the weekend after the season, and everyone wants to know what the league is like.

scenarios.title: A College Teammate's Wedding
scenarios.premise: Your old college roommate is getting married, and he wants you to give a toast.

scenarios.title: The Locker Room Fight
scenarios.premise: Two starters are swinging at each other by the cold tub, and the rookies are watching you.
scenarios.note: Repeatable (cooldown 15-20 weeks).

scenarios.title: The Quarterback's Ego
scenarios.premise: The franchise quarterback blames the special teams in a press conference.

scenarios.title: The Veteran Who Can't Let Go
scenarios.premise: A thirty-six-year-old linebacker is getting cut, and he hasn't figured it out yet.

scenarios.title: The Players-Only Meeting
scenarios.premise: The team captains call a meeting about the coach, and they want your vote.

scenarios.title: The Player Rep
scenarios.premise: The team needs a union representative, and nobody wants to be the one management remembers.

scenarios.title: The Labor Fight
scenarios.premise: The league and the union are fighting over the next agreement, and the owners are talking about replacement players.
scenarios.note: Told through teammates; no strike mechanic.

scenarios.title: The Injured Teammate
scenarios.premise: A teammate who tore his knee for the team is cut the day he's cleared to practice.

scenarios.title: The Owner's Gala
scenarios.premise: Black tie, the owner's charity, and a donor who wants a photo and a favor.

scenarios.title: The Podcast
scenarios.premise: A popular podcast wants you for an hour. The host is known for getting athletes to say too much.

scenarios.title: The Autograph Session
scenarios.premise: A mall signing goes three hours over, and the line still wraps around the food court.
scenarios.note: Repeatable (cooldown 15-20 weeks).

scenarios.title: The Awards Show
scenarios.premise: The league's awards show wants you on the red carpet the night before a practice you can't miss.

scenarios.title: The National Deal
scenarios.premise: A national brand wants you for a commercial that would play during every game this year.

scenarios.title: The Leak
scenarios.premise: Someone is leaking locker-room conversations to a reporter, and the coaches think it's a specialist.

scenarios.title: The Specialists' Dinner
scenarios.premise: The kicker, the punter and the snapper have a weekly dinner, and a new punter wants in.

scenarios.title: The Playoff Push
scenarios.premise: The city has noticed the team. Everyone wants a piece of the players in the last month.
scenarios.note: No results; the push is the atmosphere. Repeatable (cooldown 15-20 weeks).

scenarios.title: A Season Going Nowhere
scenarios.premise: The season's slipping away, and the locker room has started counting days until the offseason.
scenarios.note: Repeatable (cooldown 15-20 weeks).

scenarios.title: The Trick Play
scenarios.premise: The new coordinator wants a fake field goal with you throwing the pass, and you haven't thrown a ball since high school.

scenarios.title: After the Game
scenarios.premise: A teammate's night out after a home game starts at a club and ends somewhere you don't want to be.
scenarios.note: Strike. Clean no.

scenarios.title: The Supplement Sponsor
scenarios.premise: A supplement company offers you a deal for a product the league hasn't approved.

scenarios.title: The Video
scenarios.premise: Someone at a bar is filming you while a stranger tries to start a fight.

scenarios.title: The Friend Who Bets
scenarios.premise: An old friend who bets on games asks what you know about the starting quarterback's ankle.
scenarios.note: Integrity strike: the worst one.

scenarios.title: The Party House
scenarios.premise: A teammate rents a house for the bye week, and the guest list is long.

scenarios.title: The New Car
scenarios.premise: Your new car does zero to sixty in three seconds, and the highway is empty at midnight.

scenarios.title: The Rant
scenarios.premise: It's two in the morning and you've written four paragraphs about the general manager.

scenarios.title: The Card Game
scenarios.premise: The card game in the back of the team plane has a buy-in bigger than your first car.

scenarios.title: The Team Fine
scenarios.premise: The club fines you and calls you in. The special teams coach is there, and so is the general manager.
scenarios.note: Both choices set pro_warning (the fine is on record); owning it also sets pro_owned_it. College flags set severity through a locked choice. Every choice clears every pro strike.

scenarios.title: League Discipline
scenarios.premise: The league office wants a meeting. It's not a conversation; it's a hearing.
scenarios.note: Opens on the warning plus a new pro strike. suspend_weeks 2 (longer once R9 lands). Every choice clears every pro strike.

scenarios.title: The Last Warning, Pro
scenarios.premise: The general manager says it plainly: one more and you're done here.
scenarios.note: Every choice clears every pro strike. College last_chance adds a locked line.

scenarios.title: Released for Conduct
scenarios.premise: After a last chance, another strike: the club is done with you.
scenarios.note: Sets the dismissal flag; the release happens at season end once R7 lands.

scenarios.title: The Long Way Back, Pro
scenarios.premise: A new club, a short contract, and a list of conditions longer than the playbook.

scenarios.title: The League's Counselor
scenarios.premise: The league assigns you a counselor after the hearing, and the first session is Tuesday.

scenarios.title: A Clean Year
scenarios.premise: A full year without a fine, a headline or a hearing. The general manager notices.

scenarios.title: Thirty
scenarios.premise: You turn thirty in camp, and the trainer starts talking about 'maintenance'.

scenarios.title: The Maintenance Bill
scenarios.premise: Holding on to your leg costs more every year: more treatment, more rest, more skill points.

scenarios.title: The Younger Kicker in Camp
scenarios.premise: The club drafts a kicker in the fourth round, and he's sitting in your seat in the meeting room.

scenarios.title: The One-Year Deal
scenarios.premise: The offer is one year, the minimum, and a phone call that says take it or leave it.

scenarios.title: The Veteran Minimum
scenarios.premise: You're making a third of what you made five years ago, and the rookie next to you has your old car.

scenarios.title: The Body Says No
scenarios.premise: Your hip takes an hour to warm up now, and Monday mornings take two.

scenarios.title: The Retirement Talk
scenarios.premise: Your partner asks, gently, how many more seasons.
scenarios.note: Partner version; a single player gets the same question in PRO_149 What's Next.

scenarios.title: The Farewell Season
scenarios.premise: Do you tell the world this is your last season, or let it end quietly?
scenarios.note: The retirement itself is the player's choice on the contract screen.

scenarios.title: The General Manager's Office
scenarios.premise: The general manager says they're going in a different direction at kicker next season.
scenarios.note: Foreshadows the engine's release; retention lags a season.

scenarios.title: The Comeback Workout
scenarios.premise: Released last spring, signed this summer: everyone in camp thinks you're finished.

scenarios.title: The Broadcast Booth
scenarios.premise: A network offers you a job in the booth when you're done.

scenarios.title: The Coaching Offer
scenarios.premise: A college asks if you'd coach their kickers when you retire.

scenarios.title: Forty
scenarios.premise: You turn forty in camp. The rookies were in diapers when you kicked in high school.

scenarios.title: The Oldest Player in the League
scenarios.premise: A reporter writes that you're the oldest player in the league, and asks how long.

scenarios.title: The Last Contract
scenarios.premise: This contract is probably the last one, and your agent says so out loud.

scenarios.title: Your Kid Wants to Kick
scenarios.premise: Your kid wants to kick in middle school, and asks you to teach them.

scenarios.title: The Ring of Honor
scenarios.premise: The club wants to put your name in the stadium's ring of honor after you retire.

scenarios.title: Cleaning Out the Locker
scenarios.premise: You're cleaning out a locker after a release for the first time, and nobody walks by.
scenarios.note: At the new club, about the old one.

scenarios.title: What's Next
scenarios.premise: Your agent, your partner and your accountant all ask the same question in the same week.

scenarios.title: The Note in the Locker
scenarios.premise: A rookie leaves a note in your locker: he grew up watching you.
scenarios.note: Age 38 is reachable now (the cap retires a player after the age-38 season); ages above wait on R1.

scenarios.title: Someone New
scenarios.premise: You're single in a new city, or the person you dated in college has followed you here, and it's starting to feel serious.
scenarios.note: One scene for both paths: a player who ended things with the high school love interest meets someone new; a player who dated the college classmate makes the classmate the pro partner (locked choice). Committing re-points {love_interest} to the new partner (R8). Repeats after a breakup or divorce (cooldown 15 weeks).

scenarios.title: The Setup
scenarios.premise: A teammate's wife has decided you need to meet her friend, and dinner is Saturday whether you like it or not.
scenarios.note: Single, dating around; no cheating framing.

scenarios.title: The Profile
scenarios.premise: Someone screenshots your dating profile and it ends up on a fan account with a caption you didn't write.

scenarios.title: The Famous Date
scenarios.premise: You're photographed at dinner with someone famous, and by morning the internet has decided you're engaged.
scenarios.note: Followers up; the date has opinions about your schedule.

scenarios.title: The Fan
scenarios.premise: A fan who's been at every signing this season slips you a hotel key card with your autograph.
scenarios.note: Dating stage. Strike: pro_cheated.

scenarios.title: The Hotel Bar
scenarios.premise: After a road game, the team hotel's bar. Someone who isn't {love_interest} has been talking to you for an hour and doesn't want the night to end.
scenarios.note: Committed stage (still with the high school love interest). Tone-check scene.

scenarios.title: The Sponsor's Rep
scenarios.premise: The rep from your biggest sponsor has handled your account for a year. Tonight the dinner is just the two of you, and she suggests a nightcap at her hotel.
scenarios.note: Engaged stage. Going public costs the sponsor (scandal).

scenarios.title: The Teammate's Friend
scenarios.premise: A teammate's friend keeps showing up at the team's Thursday dinners, and keeps sitting next to you.
scenarios.note: Married stage.

scenarios.title: The Long Week on the Road
scenarios.premise: Two road games back to back, ten days from home, and a woman at the team hotel who knows exactly who you are and doesn't care that you're married.
scenarios.note: Married with kids. The kids appear only in the text.

scenarios.title: Found Out
scenarios.premise: {love_interest} has your phone in one hand and a question in the other.
scenarios.note: Story event, soon after the strike. Confess: costs now, keeps the door open. Lie: worse when it surfaces.

scenarios.title: The Lie Comes Out
scenarios.premise: The story you told {love_interest} has just fallen apart, in a text from someone you've never met.
scenarios.note: Breaking up clears every partner flag (made_long_distance_work, committed_to_relationship, new_partner, engaged).

scenarios.title: Starting Over, Together
scenarios.premise: {love_interest} agrees to see a counselor with you. The first session is Thursday, and the counselor asks who wants to go first.

scenarios.title: The Divorce
scenarios.premise: The lawyers have the paperwork ready, and {love_interest} wants to talk before anyone signs anything.
